definition: Evaluation models that score semantic similarity using embeddings (BERTScore) or are trained on human quality judgments (COMET).
details: Evaluation models that score semantic similarity using embeddings (BERTScore) or are trained on human quality judgments (COMET). Correlate far better with humans than n-gram metrics; the modern default for translation quality.

explainer.lead: Learned metrics are evaluation models that score semantic similarity using embeddings or training on human quality judgments. They matter because they correlate far better with humans than n-gram metrics and are the modern default for translation quality.

tiers.eli5: Instead of checking whether two sentences share the exact same words, these scorers ask whether they mean the same thing, much like a person would.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers swap out n-gram scores like BLEU for BERTScore or COMET when judging translations or generated text. A pitfall is trusting a metric trained on judgments from a different domain or language than the one being evaluated.
tiers.paperLevel: Similarity is computed from embedding representations (as in BERTScore) or from models trained to predict human quality ratings (as in COMET). Correlation with human judgment is far higher than n-gram metrics, but scores are only as reliable as their training judgments.

explainer.example: A COMET model scores a machine translation against a reference by predicting a human quality rating rather than counting overlapping words.
